title: HB1272 (2019 Regular): Domestic violence; prohibit those convicted of from carrying weapons.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2019/html/HB/1200-1299/HB1272IN.htm)
provenance.note: Introduced text, as filed. No passage vote is recorded for this bill. Only the words 'domestic violence or' are added; the title says 'carrying' but the text bars possession. The penalty in (2) is existing law.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Miss. Code § 97-37-5): (1) It shall be unlawful for any person who has been convicted of domestic violence or a felony under the laws of this state, any other state, or of the United States to possess any firearm or any bowie knife, dirk knife, butcher knife, switchblade knife, metallic knuckles, blackjack, or any muffler or silencer for any firearm unless such person has received a pardon for such felony, has received a relief from disability pursuant to Section 925(c) of Title 18 of the United States Code, or has received a certificate of rehabilitation pursuant to subsection (3) of this section.
Section 1 (Miss. Code § 97-37-5): (2) Any person violating this section shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not more than Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00), or committed to the custody of the State Department of Corrections for not less than one (1) year nor more than ten (10) years, or both.
